title: Topology-based machine-learning screening leads to amorphous Li5SbS3I2 solid electrolyte
summary: A LightGBM model on local structure order parameters, trained on 171 Li-containing compounds, distinguished ionic conductivity with over 70% test accuracy; SHAP analysis linked quasi-linear Li migration pathways to high conductivity. It screened 3,664 unlabeled compounds for 778 candidates, narrowed by persistent-homology clustering and molecular dynamics on 72 candidates, and Li5SbS3I2 was chosen for experiments. The crystalline phase conducted 8.6e-8 S/cm, and mechanical amorphization raised this to 8.1e-5 S/cm at 25 C, with charge-discharge tests in all-solid-state batteries. The training set is small and the conductivity is moderate.
ai_technology: LightGBM model on local structure order parameters with persistent-homology clustering for candidate screening
organization: Soochow University; Institute of Science Tokyo

evidence.tested: Li5SbS3I2 was synthesized, conductivity measured and amorphous material tested in all-solid-state cells.
evidence.unknown: Performance of the other screened candidates and competitiveness with known electrolytes; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient-boosting model screened thousands of compounds and nominated the tested candidate.
